p1.explanation: Sounds like a parody, but it's word for word from NPR. Princeton neuroscientists really staged 'gladiator style' mouse fights, and the paper is in Nature.
p1.con_line_false_alarm: Real. Princeton built a mouse colosseum, and I didn't have to invent a thing. Frankly insulting.

p2.tell: The bars compare Apr 2025, before the summer spike, with Jul 2026, 15 months later, on an axis that starts at 19¢. Same month a year apart, Jul 2025 vs. Jul 2026, prices went from 25.11 to 25.19¢ (+0.3%).
p2.explanation: Real EIA numbers, framed to mislead. Comparing a spring month with a summer month 15 months later turns the 2025 jump into a 'one year' rise, and the axis from 19¢ makes a 26.5% gap look like a cliff. Over the past year, prices have been nearly flat.
p2.con_line_fooled: Real EIA numbers. I put April 2025 next to July 2026 and started the axis at 19¢. Two choices. I'm framing this.
p2.con_line_caught: April 2025 to July 2026 is fifteen months, not one year, and my 19¢ axis didn't fool you either. Rude.

p3.explanation: Real. The account is brand new and very excited, but both numbers match BLS average prices exactly, the axis starts at zero, and per pound, coffee has cost more than ground beef every month since at least Jan 2022.
p3.con_line_false_alarm: Real. Every number is straight from BLS. Caps lock isn't a crime. Doubting the truth is my job.

p4.tell: NPR's headline says 132 years, not 32. The magazine was published in 1894.
p4.explanation: One number was swapped, and it made the story less weird. The real magazine, from 1894, came back about 132 years overdue after a New Hampshire library announced a fine freeze. A believable number is still a wrong number.
p4.con_line_fooled: One number. 132 became 32. I made the truth less weird and you relaxed. I'm framing this.
p4.con_line_caught: 132 years, not 32. The truth was weirder than my lie, and you knew it.

diff.original: Overdue library magazine returned after 132 years

p5.tell: The 85% is over a decade: NPR's sentence says 'from a decade earlier.' Over one year, Sep 2025 to Sep 2026, ground beef rose 7.4%.
p5.explanation: Every number is real, but four words are gone. 'An 85% jump' now reads like this year's price shock; NPR's sentence measures it from a decade earlier. BLS: $3.665 a pound in Sep 2016, $6.323 in Sep 2025, $6.792 in Sep 2026.
p5.con_line_fooled: I deleted 'from a decade earlier.' Four words, ten years. I'm framing this.
p5.con_line_caught: The 85% lost 'from a decade earlier,' and you noticed. Ten years squeezed into one post, unsqueezed. Rude.
